jobs.jd:
Re.Group is an Australian-owned company focused on providing solutions for recycling and recovery of resources from waste.
About the Role: As a Reliability Engineer, you will be responsible for improving equipment reliability, maintenance systems, site performance and personnel capability, developing strategies to improve equipment availability, safety and maintenance processes.
Key Responsibilities:
- Collaborate across the maintenance function to continuously improve and optimise safety, maintenance processes, operational efficiency, productivity and R & M costs.
- Improve equipment reliability through process improvement, monitoring and analysis of equipment operation, maintenance and failures, and bad actor analysis with a focus on leading KPIs.
- Enhance the technical competency of the maintenance function to support increasing equipment complexity and new technologies.
- Identify, assess and quantify opportunities to improve processes and equipment performance.
- Support site operations by interpreting OEM technical manuals and drawings and provide data-driven planning and reporting using the MEX Computerised Maintenance Management System.
- Lead RCA investigations for technical issues resulting in equipment issues and plant downtime.
- Liaise with third-party suppliers to coordinate technical support, critical maintenance activities and onsite supervision; verify completed work and ensure equipment is safely handed over to operations.
- Manage small local improvement projects as requested.
- Ensure all PM and CM activities are accurately recorded in MEX.
- Maintain the MEX asset register and stores module, ensuring asset details, maintenance schedules, inventory records and spare parts data are accurate and up to date.
- Conduct monthly stocktakes, monitor stock levels and reorder points, and ensure critical spare parts are available.
About You:
- Strong health and safety focus.
- Mechanical or Industrial Engineering qualifications.
- 3+ years' maintenance experience in recycling, manufacturing or heavy mechanical industries.
- Ability to read and interpret OEM equipment manuals, technical documents and drawings.
- Ability to lead and motivate staff and third-party contractors.
- Willing to work weekends during shutdowns and major project installations, equipment refurbishments and commissioning activities.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Based in Laverton North at our Pipe Road chemical manufacturing facility, we're looking to engage a Senior Project Engineer with mechanical specialisation within our Project Management Team. jobs.jd:

news.h: Victoria funds $15M of regional industrial infrastructure
news.p: The state is backing ten regional projects, including a water pipeline upgrade at Parwan near Bacchus Marsh that could open up to 190 hectares of industrial land for manufacturing and food processing.

news.h: Canberra consults on mandatory low-carbon fuel purchases
news.p: The federal government is seeking views on requiring fuel suppliers to buy or supply set volumes of low-carbon liquid fuels such as biofuels, aiming to lift local demand and fuel resilience.

news.h: Ampol Lytton margins surge but extended maintenance trims Q4 output
news.p: Ampol's Lytton refiner margin more than doubled year on year in the September quarter, but extended cracking-unit maintenance will cut about 150 million litres of higher-value fuel output, with restart expected mid-November.

news.h: SunRice to build rice cake plant in Leeton with federal funding
news.p: Canberra is putting $14.5 million, matched by SunRice, into a new rice processing facility at Leeton in the Riverina, supporting more than 200 jobs.

news.h: $21.6M food manufacturing expansions in Melbourne's north
news.p: The Victorian Government is backing food manufacturers in Melbourne's north with combined investments of $21.6 million to lift production and exports and add almost 50 jobs.

news.h: Project Ceres passes 79% construction
news.p: Perdaman's 2.3 Mt/yr urea plant on the Burrup is 85% complete overall, with the Saipem–Clough joint venture as EPC contractor. Perdaman is now recruiting its operations engineers.

news.h: Viva's Geelong renewable diesel gains ISCC+ certification
news.p: Co-processing of renewable feedstocks at the Geelong refinery is in its initial phase, with an expansion study under way.

news.h: NSW endorses five fuel-security projects
news.p: Southern Oil's Wagga re-refinery, Bomen biomethane, Quantem's Botany expansion and Vopak's SAF-capable aviation fuel tanks are among the projects backed by the state.

news.h: Western Sydney Aerotropolis private investment reaches $34.6B
news.p: The Bradfield Development Authority reports $34.6 billion of private investment, with new advanced manufacturing and technology facilities expanding the region's industrial base.

news.h: Jet Zero raises funds to finish FEED and approach FID
news.p: Jet Zero Australia closed a funding round backed by Qantas, Airbus and others to complete front-end engineering design for Project Ulysses; POSCO International joined as investor and the project received its final development permit.

news.h: Nufarm to close Kwinana and expand Laverton
news.p: Nufarm will stop manufacturing at Kwinana in WA by May 2027 and move about 20 million litres a year of production to its Laverton plant in Victoria.

news.h: Emissions rules now credit co-processed biofuels at refineries
news.p: Revised NGER rules let renewable content co-processed at existing refineries count as zero Scope 1 emissions, supporting Viva's plan to run Cleanaway used cooking oil through Geelong.

news.h: Australia to study its first new oil refinery in 60 years
news.p: The federal and WA governments are funding a $4 million feasibility study with Perdaman for a refinery in Western Australia. No site has been named.

news.h: ARENA backs forestry by-products for jet fuel
news.p: Up to $32 million in conditional funding for a project converting forestry residues into sustainable aviation fuel.

news.h: Mars opens $112.6 million pet food plant in Wodonga
news.p: Mars has commissioned a wet cat food pouch facility in Wodonga, Victoria, able to make up to 290 million pouches a year, with state support through Regional Development Victoria.

news.h: ARENA to run the $1.1 billion Cleaner Fuels Program
news.p: The program funds local production of renewable diesel and SAF over the next decade, aimed at freight, aviation and heavy transport.

news.h: GrainCorp eyes a $500 million crush plant to feed Lytton
news.p: GrainCorp is weighing sites for a plant of up to 1 Mt/yr to supply canola oil to the proposed Brisbane Renewable Fuels refinery with Ampol and IFM.

news.h: Queensland puts $25 million into Ampol's renewable diesel
news.p: Lytton will co-process tallow and canola oil into up to 20 ML/yr of renewable diesel from 2028, with construction from 2027. A second stage could reach 750 ML/yr in the early 2030s.

news.h: Victoria backs $92 million George Weston flour mill expansion in Ballarat
news.p: The Victorian Investment Fund is supporting a $92 million upgrade of George Weston Foods' Ballarat flour mill, adding new milling technology and about 47 jobs.

news.h: An $11 billion refinery is proposed for Gladstone
news.p: Resilient Energy Australia has secured 400 ha for a 210,000 bbl/day refinery producing mostly diesel. Queensland is in talks with several developers.

news.h: Fire hits the Geelong refinery
news.p: A fire at Viva Energy's Corio refinery, one of only two left in Australia, slowed production during a global fuel shock.

news.h: Ampol pushes back the Lytton turnaround
news.p: Scheduled maintenance at the 109,000 bbl/day refinery moves to August 2026 for about six weeks.

news.h: South Australia to host HAMR's SAF plant
news.p: HAMR Energy's planned $700–800 million methanol-to-jet facility has state government backing. The site is still being selected.

news.h: HAMR Energy raises $10 million for Portland methanol-to-jet plant
news.p: Qantas, Airbus and thyssenkrupp Uhde's SAF fund backed HAMR Energy's Series A, supporting its Portland Renewable Fuels project in Victoria targeting over 135 million litres of SAF a year.

news.h: Cargill lodges plans for a 1.1 Mt canola plant in WA
news.p: Project Crux would sit next to CBH's Kwinana Grain Terminal. WA grows more than half of Australia's canola but crushes only about a tenth of it.

news.h: Jet Zero's Project Ulysses wins environmental approval
news.p: The 113 ML/yr alcohol-to-jet plant in Townsville would be Australia's first. Jet Zero is targeting a final investment decision in 2026.
